userStories.title: Classified verdicts
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Require classified findings from both flow review tasks and retain class-specific fix/question text.

**Motivation** — A real flow therefore almost never reaches `RUN`.

**Approach** — `FlowFinding` and `parseFlowVerdict` (`apps/api/src/fleet/flows/flow-verdict.ts`). Target: `FlowFinding { id?: string; class: FlowFindingClass; summary: string; fix?: string; question?: string }` with `FlowFindingClass = 'answered' | 'minor' | 'ambiguous'`. A finding whose `class` is missing or not one of the three, an `answered`/`minor` finding without a non-blank string `fix`, or an `ambiguous` finding without a non-blank string `question` makes the whole verdict unreadable (`{ ok: false }`).

`formatFindings` (same file). Target: entries `<n>. [<id>] (<class>) <summary>`; the 2,000-character cap is unchanged.

The verdict instruction appended to both review tasks:
```text
When you are done, end your reply with exactly one JSON object on its own line, with no text after it:
{"findings":[{"id":"<short id>","class":"answered|minor|ambiguous","summary":"<one sentence>","fix":"<the change, for answered and minor>","question":"<the question, for ambiguous>"}]}
Classes: "answered" = the spec, the brainstorm or the code already settles it; "minor" = a small call you can make
and record; "ambiguous" = only the user can settle it, because the answer changes what gets built.
Use {"findings":[]} when you found nothing that should change before the next step.
{"findings":[]}
```

Update flow-verdict.spec.ts findings fixtures to include class and required text and expected class labels; missing JSON, trailing text and non-array findings keep their expectations. Update flow-steps.spec.ts from F3's two-field example to the classified example while retaining the final empty-verdict line. Update the existing strict-stop fixtures in flow-step-decision.spec.ts with `class: 'minor'` and a fix so they still expect review_findings and formatFindings detail. The existing thread-entry integration case 'a SPEC_REVIEW finding stops the flow' gains `"class":"minor","fix":"f"` and retains review_findings. Do not yet change the decision policy.

**Scope** — In: finding types, parsing/formatting, both review prompts and dependent fixture compatibility. Out: calls block construction (US-002), classified transition rules (US-005), calls application (US-006/007). Classifying `REVIEW` (PR review) findings; `REVIEW` and `FIX` jobs are dispatched exactly as in F3.

**Interface**
```typescript
export type FlowFindingClass = 'answered' | 'minor' | 'ambiguous';
export interface FlowFinding { id?: string; class: FlowFindingClass; summary: string; fix?: string; question?: string }
export function parseFlowVerdict(output: string | null | undefined): FlowVerdict;
export function formatFindings(findings: readonly FlowFinding[]): string;
```
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] parseFlowVerdict('ok\n{"findings":[{"id":"F1","class":"minor","summary":"s","fix":"f"}]}') returns ok true with the finding { id: 'F1', class: 'minor', summary: 's', fix: 'f' }.
[unit] parseFlowVerdict of a verdict with one ambiguous finding carrying question: 'q' returns ok true with that finding's class ambiguous and question q.
[unit] parseFlowVerdict of a verdict with one answered finding carrying fix: 'f' returns ok true with class answered.
[unit] parseFlowVerdict of a verdict whose only finding has no class returns { ok: false }.
[unit] parseFlowVerdict of a verdict whose only finding has class: 'major' returns { ok: false }.
[unit] parseFlowVerdict of a verdict with a minor finding and no fix returns { ok: false }.
[unit] parseFlowVerdict of a verdict with an answered finding whose fix is '   ' returns { ok: false }.
[unit] parseFlowVerdict of a verdict with an ambiguous finding and no question returns { ok: false }.
[unit] parseFlowVerdict('{"findings":[]}') still returns { ok: true, findings: [] }.
[unit] formatFindings([{ id: 'F1', class: 'minor', summary: 'Missing AC', fix: 'add it' }]) returns '1 finding: 1. [F1] (minor) Missing AC'.
[unit] formatFindings([{ class: 'answered', summary: 'S', fix: 'f' }]) (no id) returns '1 finding: 1. (answered) S'.
[unit] FLOW_VERDICT_INSTRUCTION includes the text '"class":"answered|minor|ambiguous"'.
[unit] FLOW_VERDICT_INSTRUCTION still ends with the line '{"findings":[]}'.
[unit] parseFlowVerdict('{"findings":[]} thanks') still returns { ok: false }, preserving rejection of trailing text after a verdict.
[unit] formatFindings returns exactly 2,000 characters ending in '…' when classified findings exceed FLOW_STOP_DETAIL_MAX, preserving the existing detail cap.

routing.reasoning: Pure parser/prompt changes and fixture migrations using established Vitest patterns; no authorization or token behavior changes.

modifiedFiles.reason: its findings fixtures have no `class`, which now makes a verdict unreadable; give each fixture finding a `class` (and the `fix` or `question` that class needs) and expect `formatFindings` entries with the `(<class>)` part; the cases for missing JSON, trailing text and non-array findings keep their expectations.
the instruction assertions pin F3's two-field example; they now expect the classified example with `class`, `fix` and `question`, and still expect the final `{"findings":[]}` line.

the strict-stop cases feed class-less findings (`{"id":"F1","summary":"Missing AC"}`, `{"summary":"Update plan"}`), which now parse as unreadable; give each `class: 'minor'` and a `fix` so they keep expecting `review_findings` with the `formatFindings` detail.
the "a SPEC_REVIEW finding stops the flow" case's agent output gains `"class":"minor","fix":"f"` on its finding; its flow is thread-entry, so it keeps expecting `review_findings`.

userStories.title: The calls block
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Build bounded, append-only, idempotent flow calls blocks and format ambiguous questions in a pure module.

**Motivation** — Under F3's strict stop, `/spec-review` found something on almost every pass: two of three spec reviews and the one PRD review stopped the flow, all on hygiene or coverage findings the reviewer itself called minor.

**Approach** — **At most 20 findings per review are applied** (`FLOW_CALLS_MAX_FINDINGS`); a verdict with more stops as `review_findings`. Each finding's summary and fix are collapsed to one line and cut at 1,000 characters (`FLOW_CALL_TEXT_MAX`) in the calls block. The decision policy owns rejecting excessive findings; this story supplies the constant and formatter.

**Idempotent commit.** Each review's block has the heading `### <STEP> job <jobId>`. If the spec at the branch head already contains that heading (a crash after the commit, before the record), no second commit is made and the branch head is recorded instead. This module reports alreadyApplied so US-006 can implement that commit behavior.

The calls block (appended after a blank line; the `## Flow's calls` heading only when the spec has none):
```markdown
## Flow's calls

### SPEC_REVIEW job cmw66x5ix002f08p2kcxvye58

- **ac-untagged** (minor): All 7 ACs carry no mechanism tag. Call: append [unit] to each AC.
- **2** (answered): The -0 bound is untested. Call: add an AC for clamp(-5, -0, 0).
```

A finding without an id is named by its 1-based position in the verdict; an id is collapsed to one line and cut at `FLOW_CALL_ID_MAX` (64) characters, so it can never write a heading line. Only `answered` and `minor` findings appear. A new block always goes at the end of the file, even when other text follows an existing `## Flow's calls` heading.

New symbols: `FLOW_CALLS_HEADING` (`## Flow's calls`), `FLOW_CALLS_MAX_FINDINGS` (20), `FLOW_CALL_TEXT_MAX` (1000), `FLOW_CALL_ID_MAX` (64), `formatQuestions(findings)`, `callsOutcomeForForgeError(reason: string): 'failed' | 'retry'`, `buildFlowCalls(specText: string, input: { step: 'SPEC_REVIEW' | 'PRD_REVIEW'; jobId: string; findings: FlowFinding[] }): { text: string; alreadyApplied: boolean }`.

`formatQuestions` lists ambiguous findings' question strings using numbered entries and optional ids, singular/plural question prefix, and the same 2,000-character cap with a final ellipsis when truncated. A `RepoCheckException`: `callsOutcomeForForgeError(reason)` is `failed` (detail = the reason) for `app_not_installed`, `app_permissions_insufficient` and `repo_not_found`, `retry` for any other reason. Any other error propagates in the service, not in this pure mapper.

**Scope** — In: pure constants, calls text builder, questions formatter, forge-reason outcome mapping and co-located unit specs. Out: verdict parsing (US-001), persistence (US-003), decision enforcement (US-005), forge writes (US-004/006). Rewriting the spec body: calls are only appended under `## Flow's calls`; no finding edits an existing line.

**Interface**
```typescript
export function callsOutcomeForForgeError(reason: string): 'failed' | 'retry';
export function buildFlowCalls(specText: string, input: { step: 'SPEC_REVIEW' | 'PRD_REVIEW'; jobId: string; findings: FlowFinding[] }): { text: string; alreadyApplied: boolean };
```
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] buildFlowCalls('# Spec\n', { step: 'SPEC_REVIEW', jobId: 'j1', findings: [{ id: 'a', class: 'minor', summary: 'S', fix: 'F' }] }) returns alreadyApplied false.

[unit] For that call, the returned text ends with the seven lines: blank, '## Flow's calls', blank, '### SPEC_REVIEW job j1', blank, '- **a** (minor): S Call: F' and a final empty line, after the unchanged '# Spec\n'.

[unit] buildFlowCalls of a spec that already contains the line '## Flow's calls' adds only the '### <STEP> job <jobId>' block at the end of the file, so '## Flow's calls' appears once in the returned text.
[unit] buildFlowCalls of a spec that already contains the line '### PRD_REVIEW job j2', called with step: 'PRD_REVIEW' and jobId: 'j2', returns alreadyApplied true and the spec text unchanged.
[unit] buildFlowCalls with a finding that has no id names it by its 1-based position in the findings list ('- **2** (answered): ...' for the second finding).
[unit] buildFlowCalls with an id of 'x\n### SPEC_REVIEW job j9' writes the id on one line inside the bullet, so the returned text has no line equal to '### SPEC_REVIEW job j9'.
[unit] buildFlowCalls with a finding of class ambiguous among minor ones leaves the ambiguous finding out of the block.
[unit] buildFlowCalls with a summary containing a newline writes the summary on one line, the newline replaced by a space.
[unit] buildFlowCalls with a 3,000-character fix writes a bullet whose text after 'Call: ' is 1,000 (FLOW_CALL_TEXT_MAX) characters long.
[unit] buildFlowCalls with a 100-character id writes a bullet whose bold id is 64 (FLOW_CALL_ID_MAX) characters long.
[unit] formatQuestions([{ id: 'q1', class: 'ambiguous', summary: 's', question: 'Which DB?' }]) returns '1 question: 1. [q1] Which DB?'.
[unit] formatQuestions of two ambiguous findings returns a text starting with '2 questions: '.
[unit] formatQuestions of questions whose joined text exceeds 2,000 characters returns at most 2,000 characters ending in '…'.
[unit] callsOutcomeForForgeError('app_permissions_insufficient') returns 'failed'.
[unit] callsOutcomeForForgeError('provider_error') returns 'retry'.

routing.reasoning: A single additive pure source module formats bounded text and detects exact headings; co-located TDD needs neither I/O fixtures nor new infrastructure.

userStories.title: Calls and ticket columns
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Persist the last applied calls job and the flow's ticket, and expose the transactional repository operations needed by later stories.

**Motivation** — F3 left stops silent (`stopReason` and `stopDetail` only).

**Approach** — `FleetFlowFeatureRecord` and `FleetFlowRecord` (`apps/api/src/fleet/flows/domain/fleet-flow.domain.ts`). Target: the feature adds optional `callsJobId?: string | null`; the flow adds optional `ticketId?: string | null`.

`IFleetFlowStepRepository` (`apps/api/src/fleet/flows/domain/fleet-flow-step.domain.ts`) and `PrismaFleetFlowStepRepository`. Target: adds `countJobsForStepSince(flowId: string, step: FlowStep, since: Date): Promise<number>` (jobs with `queuedAt` at or after `since`), `projectSlug(projectId: string): Promise<string | null>` (null when the project is gone or soft-deleted), `recordCalls(flowId: string, featureId: string, jobId: string, specSha: string): Promise<void>` (sets the feature's `callsJobId` and the flow's `specSha`) and `setTicket(flowId: string, ticketId: string): Promise<boolean>` (sets `ticketId` only where it is null; true when it set it).

Prisma: `FleetFlowFeature.callsJobId String?`; `FleetFlow.ticketId String?` with a relation to `Ticket` (`onDelete: SetNull`) and the back-relation on `Ticket`.

One migration adds `FleetFlowFeature.callsJobId` and `FleetFlow.ticketId` (relation to `Ticket`, `onDelete: SetNull`). The domain records gain both optional fields; the step repository gains `countJobsForStepSince`, `projectSlug`, `recordCalls` and `setTicket`. Create migration 20261129090000_fleet_flow_verdicts/migration.sql and a real-Postgres migration/repository integration spec. Keep the Prisma schema and SQL in sync; regenerate the gitignored Prisma client, never edit generated client files. Existing rows read null without a backfill. Update PrismaFleetFlowRepository.toDomain only as needed to carry both columns, including features. recordCalls is a paired mutation intended for the caller's existing transaction; setTicket uses a null-only conditional update rather than an unconditional overwrite. If existing repository integration tests pin full returned columns, add callsJobId and ticketId as null; nothing else changes.

**Scope** — In: nullable schema/relation/migration, domain projection, four repository methods and real database checks. Out: calls commits (US-006), engine orchestration (US-007), ticket creation/comment handling and its bookkeeping scope (US-010). Closing or transitioning the flow's ticket; it stays in its created state.

**Interface**
```typescript
countJobsForStepSince(flowId: string, step: FlowStep, since: Date): Promise<number>;
projectSlug(projectId: string): Promise<string | null>;
recordCalls(flowId: string, featureId: string, jobId: string, specSha: string): Promise<void>;
setTicket(flowId: string, ticketId: string): Promise<boolean>;
```

[integration] After the migration, a FleetFlow row inserted without ticketId reads back with ticketId null.
[integration] Deleting the Ticket a flow's ticketId points at leaves the flow row in place with ticketId null.
[integration] countJobsForStepSince(flowId, 'PLAN', since) returns 2 for a flow with two PLAN jobs queued after since and one SPEC_REVIEW job.
[integration] countJobsForStepSince(flowId, 'PLAN', since) does not count a PLAN job queued before since.
[integration] countJobsForStepSince(flowId, 'PLAN', since) returns 0 for a flow with no jobs.
[integration] projectSlug(projectId) returns the project's slug.
[integration] projectSlug(projectId) returns null for a soft-deleted project.
[integration] recordCalls(flowId, featureId, 'j1', 'abc123') sets the feature's callsJobId to 'j1'.
[integration] recordCalls(flowId, featureId, 'j1', 'abc123') sets the flow's specSha to 'abc123'.
[integration] setTicket(flowId, ticketId) on a flow with no ticket sets ticketId and returns true.
[integration] setTicket(flowId, otherTicketId) on a flow that already has a ticket leaves ticketId unchanged and returns false.

userStories.title: GitHub contents write
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add a single-file GitHub contents write through the existing bounded, no-redirect forge client.

**Motivation** — A real flow therefore almost never reaches `RUN`.

**Approach** — `GitHubAppClient` (`apps/api/src/fleet/git-broker/github-app-client.ts`). Target: adds `putFile(token, owner, name, path, input: { branch: string; content: Buffer; blobSha: string; message: string }): Promise<PutFileResult>` with `PutFileResult = { kind: 'committed'; commitSha: string } | { kind: 'conflict' } | { kind: 'refused' }` (`409` is `conflict`, `422` is `refused`).

`FleetHttpClient.request` (`apps/api/src/fleet/git-broker/fleet-http-client.ts`). Target: `method: 'GET' | 'POST' | 'PUT'`; a `PUT` sends its JSON body like a `POST`.

**Write refusals.** A `422` from the contents write (a branch rule or an invalid request) is a refusal, not a transient error: the flow stops as `calls_failed`. This client reports refused; the calls service and engine own stopping.

**Write conflicts.** A `409` from the contents write re-reads the file: if its blob sha is unchanged, the write was refused for another reason (a branch rule) and the flow stops as `calls_failed`; if it moved, this pass ends and the next tick retries against the new file. This client reports conflict; US-006 owns the re-read.

putFile sends one PUT to the segment-encoded contents path with body { message, branch, sha: blobSha, content: content.toString('base64') }. Return committed with response commit.sha on 200 or 201; malformed success payload is provider_error. Map 404 to RepoCheckException('repo_not_found'), 403 to app_permissions_insufficient, and 500 to provider_error, using the existing exception type. Keep authorization headers, configured timeout, redirect refusal and JSON handling unchanged. Test PUT/body and all status mappings with the existing fake-forge pattern; no existing expectation changes. No change to token minting scopes is needed: mintInstallationToken already has contents:write.

**Scope** — In: HTTP method union and GitHub file-replacement primitive with fake-forge tests. Out: calls text (US-002), repository/token orchestration and conflict re-read policy (US-006), advancement (US-007). GitLab repositories: flows are GitHub-only, and `putFile` exists only on the GitHub client. Signing the calls commit or setting its author: GitHub records it as the App.

**Interface**
```typescript
export type PutFileResult = { kind: 'committed'; commitSha: string } | { kind: 'conflict' } | { kind: 'refused' };
putFile(token: string, owner: string, name: string, path: string, input: { branch: string; content: Buffer; blobSha: string; message: string }): Promise<PutFileResult>;
```
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] FleetHttpClient.request('PUT', url, headers, body) sends a PUT whose JSON body reaches the fake forge unchanged.

[unit] putFile(token, 'o', 'r', '.nax/features/a/spec.md', { branch: 'feat/a', content, blobSha: 'b1', message: 'm' }) sends one PUT to '/repos/o/r/contents/.nax/features/a/spec.md' whose JSON body has message 'm', branch 'feat/a', sha 'b1' and content equal to the base64 of content.
[unit] putFile returns { kind: 'committed', commitSha } with the response's commit.sha when GitHub answers 200.
[unit] putFile returns { kind: 'committed', commitSha } when GitHub answers 201.
[unit] putFile returns { kind: 'conflict' } when GitHub answers 409.
[unit] putFile throws RepoCheckException with reason 'repo_not_found' when GitHub answers 404.
[unit] putFile throws RepoCheckException with reason 'app_permissions_insufficient' when GitHub answers 403.
[unit] putFile returns { kind: 'refused' } when GitHub answers 422.
[unit] putFile throws RepoCheckException with reason 'provider_error' when GitHub answers 500.
[unit] putFile throws RepoCheckException with reason 'provider_error' when a 200 response has no string commit.sha.
[unit] putFile with a path segment containing a space sends the segment URL-encoded.
[unit] FleetHttpClient.request('GET', url, {}) still returns { status: 200, body: { a: 1 } } when the fake forge responds with that JSON body, preserving existing GET behavior after PUT is added.
[unit] FleetHttpClient.request('POST', url, headers, body) still sends the supplied JSON body unchanged, preserving existing POST behavior after PUT is added.

userStories.title: Step decision for classified verdicts
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Select apply_calls, continuation or a precise stop using the ordered classified-review policy.

**Motivation** — A real flow therefore almost never reaches `RUN`.

**Approach** — `FlowStepInput`, `FlowStepAction`, `FlowStopReason` and `decideFlowStep` (`apps/api/src/fleet/flows/flow-step-decision.ts`). Target: the input adds `callsJobId: string | null` (the feature's last applied review job), `planCount: number` (the flow's `PLAN` jobs) and `canApplyCalls: boolean` (true for nax-entry flows); the action union adds `{ kind: 'apply_calls'; step: 'SPEC_REVIEW' | 'PRD_REVIEW'; jobId: string; findings: FlowFinding[] }`, exported as `ApplyCallsAction = Extract<FlowStepAction, { kind: 'apply_calls' }>`; stop reasons add `review_ambiguous` and `calls_failed`.

`decideFlowStep` for a `COMPLETED` review job whose verdict parsed, in this order (the first rule that matches wins):

1. No findings: `SPEC_REVIEW` continues to `PLAN`, `PRD_REVIEW` to `RUN` (unchanged from F3).
2. Any `ambiguous` finding: stop `review_ambiguous`, detail `formatQuestions` of the ambiguous findings.
3. More than `FLOW_CALLS_MAX_FINDINGS` findings: stop `review_findings`, detail `formatFindings`.
4. `canApplyCalls` false (thread entry): stop `review_findings`, detail `formatFindings`.
5. `PRD_REVIEW` with `planCount` 2 or more: stop `review_findings`, detail `formatFindings` (the second round).
6. `callsJobId` equals the job's id (calls already recorded): dispatch `PLAN`.
7. Otherwise: `apply_calls` with the job's step, id and findings.

Both reviews are classified. `PRD_REVIEW` `answered`/`minor` findings are appended to the spec as calls, then the flow re-runs `PLAN` once. A second round of `PRD_REVIEW` findings stops the flow. Empty verdicts still proceed even in round two. Invalid classified findings follow the existing verdict_unreadable path. Preserve all unrelated failure, active-job, RUN ingest, REVIEW, FIX and multi-feature decisions.

So that `apps/api` still type-checks, `FleetFlowAdvanceService.decisionInput` supplies `callsJobId: null`, `planCount: 0` and `canApplyCalls: false` until US-007 fills them. The flow-step-decision.spec.ts input fixture helper gains the same defaults (false keeps every existing strict-stop expectation, as for a thread-entry flow); new F4a cases set them explicitly.

**Scope** — In: pure decision inputs/action/stop reasons, ordered review rules and temporary engine input defaults. Out: real database input population/creator guards (US-007), forge service (US-006), stop event (US-008). `WAITING_ANSWER`, posting the batched questions on the ticket, the answers API and resuming after answers (fleet flow F4b); in F4a an `ambiguous` finding stops the flow. More than one re-plan per flow: a second `PRD_REVIEW` with findings stops the flow.

**Interface**
```typescript
// Additional FlowStepInput members:
callsJobId: string | null;
planCount: number;
canApplyCalls: boolean;
// Additional FlowStepAction member:
{ kind: 'apply_calls'; step: 'SPEC_REVIEW' | 'PRD_REVIEW'; jobId: string; findings: FlowFinding[] }
export type ApplyCallsAction = Extract<FlowStepAction, { kind: 'apply_calls' }>;
```
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] decideFlowStep for a COMPLETED SPEC_REVIEW whose verdict has one ambiguous finding returns stop review_ambiguous with the detail formatQuestions returns for it.
[unit] decideFlowStep for a COMPLETED SPEC_REVIEW with one minor and one ambiguous finding returns stop review_ambiguous (rule 2 wins over rule 7).
[unit] decideFlowStep for a COMPLETED SPEC_REVIEW with 21 minor findings and canApplyCalls true returns stop review_findings.
[unit] decideFlowStep for a COMPLETED SPEC_REVIEW with one minor finding and canApplyCalls false returns stop review_findings with the formatFindings detail.
[unit] decideFlowStep for a COMPLETED SPEC_REVIEW (job j1) with one minor finding, canApplyCalls true and callsJobId null returns apply_calls with step SPEC_REVIEW, job id j1 and that finding.
[unit] decideFlowStep for the same job with callsJobId j1 returns dispatch PLAN.
[unit] decideFlowStep for a COMPLETED PRD_REVIEW (job j2) with one answered finding, planCount 1, canApplyCalls true and callsJobId null returns apply_calls with step PRD_REVIEW and job id j2.
[unit] decideFlowStep for that PRD_REVIEW with callsJobId j2 and planCount 1 returns dispatch PLAN.
[unit] decideFlowStep for a COMPLETED PRD_REVIEW with one minor finding, canApplyCalls true and planCount 2 returns stop review_findings.
[unit] decideFlowStep for a COMPLETED PRD_REVIEW with no findings and planCount 2 returns dispatch RUN.
[unit] decideFlowStep for a COMPLETED SPEC_REVIEW with no findings still returns dispatch PLAN.
[unit] decideFlowStep for a COMPLETED SPEC_REVIEW whose output has a class-less finding returns stop verdict_unreadable.
[unit] decideFlowStep returns stop verdict_unreadable for a COMPLETED review whose finding has class 'major'.
[unit] decideFlowStep returns stop verdict_unreadable for a COMPLETED review whose answered/minor finding lacks a nonblank fix.
[unit] decideFlowStep returns stop verdict_unreadable for a COMPLETED review whose ambiguous finding lacks a nonblank question.

userStories.title: The calls service
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Append the review's calls to the remote spec with crash recovery, head validation and explicit forge outcomes.

**Motivation** — A real flow therefore almost never reaches `RUN`.

**Approach** — **Calls are appended by the api.** The verdict carries each finding's `fix`. The api commits them to the spec as a "Flow's calls" section through a new GitHub contents write (the App's installation token already has `contents: write`). No runner change; the spec body above the section is never rewritten.

**A push between the review and the calls re-asks.** Before writing, `apply` compares the branch head with the head the review saw (`expectedHead`: `flow.specSha` for `SPEC_REVIEW`, the latest `PLAN` job's `resultSha` for `PRD_REVIEW`). A different head returns `stale`, and `advance` re-asks through `FleetFlowsService.reaskLocked` with that head, exactly as the F3 spec-sha check does before `PLAN`. The check runs only when the calls block is not on the branch yet, so the crash-recovery path (block present, head = the calls commit) never trips it. US-007 supplies expectedHead and performs the re-ask; this service only returns stale.

`FleetFlowCallsService.apply` algorithm (the explicit three-argument interface below is authoritative):
1. `findReviewRepo(flow.repoId)`; missing or no installation: `failed` `repo not connected`.
2. `mintInstallationToken`, then `getFile(spec path, flow.branch)`; null: `failed` `spec missing on <branch>`.
3. `buildFlowCalls(file text, action)`; `alreadyApplied`: `committed` with `getBranchHead(flow.branch)`. Otherwise `getBranchHead(flow.branch)` must equal `expectedHead`, else `stale` with that head.
4. `putFile` with the file's blob sha and message `docs(<feature>): flow calls from <STEP> job <jobId>`; `committed`: `committed` with its commit sha; `refused`: `failed` `spec write refused`; `conflict`: `getFile` again, same blob sha: `failed` `spec write refused`, different: `retry`.

userStories.title: Advance applies calls
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Execute apply_calls outside transactions and record/re-ask/stop under existing generation-aware locks without self-invalidating the approved spec.

**Motivation** — A real flow therefore almost never reaches `RUN`.

**Approach** — `FleetFlowAdvanceService` (`apps/api/src/fleet/flows/fleet-flow-advance.service.ts`). Target: `DispatchPass.action` is `DispatchAction | ApplyCallsAction`; for `apply_calls`, `decide` runs only the creator-access guard (inside its transaction, as for a dispatch; no cap or spec-sha guard) and returns the pass; `advance` then calls `FleetFlowCallsService.apply` outside a transaction, with `expectedHead` = `flow.specSha` for `SPEC_REVIEW` or the latest `PLAN` job's `resultSha` for `PRD_REVIEW`, and records under the locks. `decide` keeps a `SPEC_REVIEW` latest job whose id is the feature's `callsJobId` and whose `queuedAt` is at or after `approvedAt`, even though its `ref` is no longer `specSha`. `readSpecHead` also reads the forge head when the latest job is a terminal `PRD_REVIEW` whose id is the feature's `callsJobId` (a re-plan follows). `decisionInput` fills the three new inputs (`planCount` counts only `PLAN` jobs queued at or after `approvedAt`).

**The flow's own spec commit never re-asks.** The calls commit moves `flow.specSha` to the new commit sha in the same transaction that records the calls, so the existing spec-sha check before `PLAN` sees its own commit as the approved spec. A later push by anyone else still re-asks.

**Thread-entry flows cannot take calls.** A thread's branch is local to its runner (thread publish never pushes), so the api cannot commit to it. A thread-entry review with `answered`/`minor` findings stops as `review_findings`, as in F3.

**The calls step is not billed** and runs no cap guard; it does run the creator-access guard (it writes to the repository on the creator's behalf).

For `apply_calls`, `decide` runs the creator-access guard under its locks (stop `creator_lost_access`) and returns the pass; `advance` calls `FleetFlowCallsService.apply` with no transaction open, then:

- `committed`: one transaction locks parent and flow (`lockLive`); if still live, `recordCalls(flowId, featureId, jobId, specSha)`, an audit entry `system.flow.advance` (summary `flow calls <STEP>`) and activity `flow.calls` `{ step, jobId, specSha, count }`. The next tick dispatches `PLAN`.
- `stale`: one transaction locks parent and flow; if still live, `reaskLocked(flow, head, now)` (the flow returns to `PENDING` with the new sha).
- `retry`: nothing is written.
- `failed`: stop `calls_failed`, detail `<STEP>: <detail>`.

The creator guard uses creatorAccess, PermissionService.effectiveKeys and mayDispatch as F3 does, but runs before returning an apply_calls pass without executing cap/spec-sha dispatch guards. Keep forge I/O outside transactions and narrow apply_calls away from dispatch-only action.pr consumers. Keep lockLive's approval-generation/state checks, so a flow that leaves APPROVED/RUNNING before the record receives no calls progress. ReadSpecHead must not read the forge for a terminal PRD_REVIEW with no findings and no callsJobId match; it proceeds to RUN as before.

Append FleetFlowCallsService after the config constructor parameter; OutboxService will be appended after it by US-008. Provide FleetFlowCallsService in FlowsModule. Update advance.service.spec.ts and advance-review.spec.ts positional constructors with the calls stub, and step repository stubs with countJobsForStepSince returning 0 and recordCalls; no existing expectation changes. Add fleet-flow-advance-calls.spec.ts entering at advance to pin the service seam and all four outcomes. flows.module.spec.ts must still compile the real module without a DB and expose FleetFlowCallsService.

**Scope** — In: engine decision/record integration, real new decision inputs, generation-aware applied-review retention, re-plan head preflight and calls service DI. Out: text/service internals (US-002/006), stop outbox event (US-008), subscribers (US-009/010), real-DB scenarios (US-011). Applying calls for thread-entry flows: their branch exists only on the runner, so the api cannot commit to it.

**Interface**
```typescript
// DispatchPass.action:
DispatchAction | ApplyCallsAction
// Calls service invoked by advance:
apply(flow: FleetFlowRecord, action: ApplyCallsAction, expectedHead: string): Promise<CallsOutcome>;
```

[unit] After apply returns committed with sha 's2', advance calls recordCalls(flowId, featureId, jobId, 's2').
[unit] After apply returns committed with sha 's2', advance records activity 'flow.calls' with { step: 'SPEC_REVIEW', jobId, specSha: 's2', count: 1 }.

userStories.description:
**Goal** — Record one bounded, validated flow-stop outbox event atomically with every engine stop.

**Motivation** — F3 left stops silent (`stopReason` and `stopDetail` only).

**Approach** — **Stop notices come from the outbox.** The engine's stop transaction records one outbox event `fleet_flow_stopped` (event id `<flowId>:stopped`). Two handlers consume it: a notifications handler (in-app and email per preference, category `FLEET_NEEDS_YOU`) and a fleet handler that creates the flow's ticket on first use and posts the stop comment. A human stop (`FleetFlowsService.stop`) and an approval rejection enqueue nothing: a human did them. This story implements the producer/shared payload only; US-009/010 implement handlers.

The stop event payload:
`{ flowId, projectId, feature, stopReason, detail (first 500 characters), approverId: string | null, creatorType: 'USER' | 'AGENT', creatorId }`.

Preserve stopDetail's 2,000-character cap and existing audit/activity; truncate only event.detail to its first 500 characters. The source feature is the flow's single feature and creatorType/creatorId come from createdByType/createdById. The parser validates all required fields and USER|AGENT creator type, preserving a valid payload's nullable approverId unchanged. userStories.description:
**Goal** — Prove classified flow progression and replay-safe stop effects through the real ticker, repositories and outbox against Postgres with stubbed GitHub I/O.

**Motivation** — A real flow therefore almost never reaches `RUN`.

**Approach** — Integration tests that run `FleetFlowTicker.tick` over real flows and jobs with a stubbed GitHub client, and the stop handlers over a real outbox row.

The US-007 → US-011 seam: `FleetFlowTicker.tick` reaches the calls commit and then dispatches `PLAN` (US-011 proves it against the database).

For a nax-entry single-feature flow with a completed classified SPEC_REVIEW, tick invokes the real engine/calls service and records the forge commit/callsJobId; a second tick with forge head equal to that commit dispatches a real PLAN job. Seed approvedAt before review queuedAt and consistent currentStep/state to enter advancement rather than a bookkeeping-only recovery tick. Stub GitHubAppClient token/file/head/putFile collaborators, not FleetFlowCallsService or decideFlowStep. Forge I/O remains outside a transaction.

For an ambiguous verdict, tick stops review_ambiguous and atomically writes one fleet_flow_stopped row, event id <flowId>:stopped. Publish that actual row through FanOutPublisher so both registered handlers run. Assert the created TASK ticket's title, flow.ticketId, stop comment and approver notification, then republish the same row and observe no duplicate ticket or comment. Existing NotificationWriter deduplication is retained. A PRD_REVIEW minor verdict with two PLAN jobs since approval stops review_findings.

Mirror test/integration/fleet/fleet-flow-advance.integration.spec.ts for tick fixtures and test/integration/nax-flow-entry.integration.spec.ts for NAX/forge setup. Put the new file at test/integration/fleet/fleet-flow-verdicts.integration.spec.ts. Use canRunDbTests() and the real test Postgres setup; run test:scoped outside NAX_SANDBOXED=1 with KODA_DB_TESTS=1. Database suites must execute, not merely compile or skip. Do not run destructive DB suites concurrently against the same test database. This binding test-only story remains separate as explicitly required by the spec.

**Scope** — In: the declared real-database ticker and outbox seam scenarios. Out: new parser/policy/forge/engine/subscriber production behaviors (US-001 through US-010), no new endpoints or runner behavior. Notifications or ticket comments for a flow's completion, for a human stop and for an approval rejection.

**Interface**
```typescript
FleetFlowTicker.tick(now: Date): Promise<void>;
FanOutPublisher.publish(record: OutboxRecord): Promise<void>;
```
acceptanceCriteria: [integration] A tick over a RUNNING nax-entry flow whose latest job is a COMPLETED SPEC_REVIEW with one minor finding, with a stubbed GitHubAppClient whose putFile returns commit 'c2', sets the feature's callsJobId to that job's id and the flow's specSha to 'c2'.
[integration] A second tick over that flow, with the stubbed forge head 'c2', inserts a PLAN job with flowId the flow's id and flowStep PLAN.
[integration] A tick over a flow whose latest SPEC_REVIEW has an ambiguous finding leaves the flow STOPPED with stopReason review_ambiguous.
[integration] That stop leaves one outbox row of type 'fleet_flow_stopped' with event id '<flowId>:stopped'.
[integration] Publishing that outbox row through FanOutPublisher creates one ticket titled 'Fleet flow: <feature>'.
[integration] After that publish, the flow's ticketId is the created ticket's id.
[integration] After that publish, the ticket has one comment starting with 'Flow stopped (review_ambiguous):'.
[integration] Publishing the same outbox row a second time creates no second ticket and no second comment.
[integration] Publishing that outbox row creates one flow_stopped notification for the approver with source type fleet_flow and source id the flow id.
[integration] A tick over a RUNNING flow whose latest job is a COMPLETED PRD_REVIEW with one minor finding and two PLAN jobs since approval leaves it STOPPED with stopReason review_findings.

FEATURE AND SUCCESS: F4a replaces F3's stop-on-any-finding policy for SPEC_REVIEW and PRD_REVIEW with classified verdicts. NAX-entry flows append answered/minor calls to the remote spec through the GitHub App, atomically record callsJobId and the calls commit as specSha, and proceed to PLAN. PRD review allows one re-plan; genuine ambiguity stops with questions. Every engine stop atomically enqueues one fleet_flow_stopped event, consumed independently for notifications and a lazily created ticket/comment. Done means the eleven binding stories and their runtime/database assertions are implemented, including tick-to-commit-to-PLAN and idempotent stop fan-out. This is an enhancement, not greenfield.

DISCOVERY AND GUIDANCE: The supplied execution root is /Users/williamkhoo/workspace/subrina-coder/projects/koda/repos/koda. codebase-memory MCP tools are not exposed, so discovery used direct source reads and text searches; no graph index was queried. The package labels in the prompt are stale: .nax/mono/apps/api/context.md:23 specifies NestJS 12 + Fastify, Prisma 7, and Vitest, not Express, and root guidance identifies Nuxt rather than Next.js. All implementation stays in apps/api. Read the app context and nathapp-nestjs-patterns skill before writing NestJS implementation; that skill was not present among the exposed repository files. This task only authors the requested PRD artifact; implementation must not change .nax rules/config or generated acceptance files.

Preserve those parsing regression anchors while requiring class and nonblank class-specific text; legacy class-less nonempty verdicts deliberately become unreadable, not implicit minor findings. formatFindings at :43 currently caps details at FLOW_STOP_DETAIL_MAX. apps/api/src/fleet/flows/flow-steps.ts:5 defines the old instruction, :10 sets the 2000-character limit, and :14 appends the instruction to both /spec-review tasks within AGENT_TASK_MAX_LENGTH. Preserve task path construction and the final empty-verdict line. flow-calls.ts is a new pure helper module; it must preserve the original spec prefix byte-for-byte, append at EOF, detect exact heading lines for idempotency, collapse id/summary/fix to one line, bound id to 64 and each text to 1000, and omit ambiguous bullets. formatQuestions carries ambiguous questions, not summaries, within 2000 characters. The decision, not the builder, enforces the 20-finding application limit.

STATE MACHINE (US-005): apps/api/src/fleet/flows/flow-step-decision.ts:20 holds FlowStepInput, :32 stop reasons, :45 the action union, and :63 decideFlowStep. The COMPLETED review branch at :101 currently stops every nonempty parsed verdict. Replace only that branch with the seven ordered rules. Empty findings win first; ambiguity precedes size/thread/round limits; round-two PRD findings stop even if callsJobId matches; recorded calls otherwise select PLAN.
